newsitem.title: UK: Dixons gains on pre-results bargain-hunting.
newsitem.headline: Dixons gains on pre-results bargain-hunting.

text.p: Shares in Dixons Group Plc gained nearly three percent on Monday, charged up by bargain hunting ahead of an expected 40 percent gain in annual profits by Britain's leading electricals retailer when it posts results on Wednesday.
By 0913 GMT, Dixons traded 13-1/2p higher at 489p, still well below this year's peak of 552p.
A newspaper report that two leading analysts were turning more positive also lifted Dixons, traders said.
The Financial Mail on Sunday said BZW retail analyst Tony Shiret was almost tempted to be a buyer.

NatWest Markets' analyst Nathan Cockrell said he was not concerned over a possible Office of Fair Trading inquiry into extended warranties, which account for less than 10 percent of profits, the newspaper said.
Market sources said NatWest rates Dixons as "add."
One analyst said Dixons benefited from buoyant UK consumer spending that showed little sign of cooling off after last week's budget from Chancellor of the Exchequer Gordon Brown.
"A few people are anticipating buying interest after the results," he said. "This is a quality stock in an oversold sector."
He expected results to be within expectations but initial comparisons to year-ago figures may look disappointing.

Strong consumer demand and weaker competition is expected to boost pre-exceptional profits to between 180 and 196.5 million stg in the year to end-April, from 135.2 million stg a year ago, analysts said.
The dividend is expected to increase to 10 to 10.8 pence a share, from 8.75 pence a share.
